provenance: author-created synthetic READMEs and repository artifacts; no real README, posting, employer or private material
authorship_disclosure: Authored by a separate Claude subagent instance given only the task, the alias/concept list, the artifact rules and the output schema; it was never shown Policy D's rules, collocates, non-use frames, code, tests or results and had no repository access. It is the same model family as the policy author, so this is NOT human-independent validation. Labels are frozen exactly as authored.
author_note: Reserve set written from scratch with fresh wording and no val1 sentences or named phrases; same labelling rules: 'used' counts README use claims plus manifest entries and language bytes of at least 5%, without inferring a language from a framework.
label_timing: labels frozen BEFORE any GitScore extractor, matcher or README policy ran on this set

repos.name: kanbanette
repos.readme:
# kanbanette

Drag-and-drop board for personal tasks. The client is a single-page React application; columns and cards are plain components whose state is persisted to IndexedDB.

## Getting started

```
npm ci
npm run start
```

controls.note: The client is described as a React application.

repos.name: thermostat-guard
repos.readme:
# thermostat-guard

Watches greenhouse sensors and texts the grower when the temperature drifts out of range. The point is to react before the seedlings cook, not after.

## Hardware

Any sensor that reports over MQTT works; tested with three cheap probes.

controls.note: 'react before the seedlings cook' means respond.

repos.name: invoicer-api
repos.readme:
# invoicer-api

REST API for issuing and tracking invoices. Routes live in `server/routes`, request validation runs before each handler, and failures fall through to a final Express error middleware that formats problem responses.

controls.note: The API's error handling is Express middleware, implying an Express server.

repos.name: ticketfare
repos.readme:
# ticketfare

Fare calculator for a regional bus network. Prices depend on the zones crossed and on whether the trip includes an express coach, which carries a fixed surcharge.

## Tariff file

Zones and surcharges are configured in `tariff.toml`.

controls.note: An express coach is a fast bus service.

repos.name: tracewalk
repos.readme:
# tracewalk

Flame-graph generator for sampled stack traces. Compiles to a single binary and is Rust all the way down, with no C dependencies to vendor.

```
tracewalk samples.txt > flame.svg
```

controls.note: 'Rust all the way down' states the implementation language.

repos.name: fleetcare
repos.readme:
# fleetcare

Service tracker for a fleet of delivery vans. Mechanics log brake wear, tyre depth and underbody rust at each inspection, and the dashboard flags vans that are due for work.

controls.note: Underbody rust is corrosion on vans.

repos.name: rakehelpers
repos.readme:
# rakehelpers

Rake tasks I keep copying between Ruby projects: database dumps, asset checksums, release tagging. Packaged as a gem.

Add it to your Gemfile and `require 'rakehelpers'` in the Rakefile.

controls.note: A gem of Rake tasks required from a Rakefile is Ruby code.

repos.name: anniversary-reminder
repos.readme:
# anniversary-reminder

Reminds you of anniversaries a week ahead and suggests the traditional gift: paper for the first year, tin for the tenth, ruby for the fortieth, gold for the fiftieth.

controls.note: Ruby is the traditional fortieth-anniversary gemstone.

repos.name: metricsd-agent
repos.readme:
# metricsd-agent

JVM agent that exports garbage-collection and thread-pool metrics in a text format scrapers understand. Compiled for Java 11 and tested on every LTS release since.

controls.note: A JVM agent compiled for Java 11.

repos.name: roastlog
repos.readme:
# roastlog

Roast profiles for a home coffee roaster. Log the bean origin, charge temperature and first crack, and roastlog charts each batch so you can compare a Kenyan against a Java or a Sumatra.

controls.note: Java here is a coffee bean origin.

repos.name: haptiq
repos.readme:
# haptiq

Haptic feedback presets for iOS apps. One-line Swift API:

```
Haptiq.play(.success)
```

Presets are tuned per device class.

controls.note: The library exposes a Swift API for iOS apps.

repos.name: fieldnotes-birding
repos.readme:
# fieldnotes-birding

Checklist app for birders. Log each sighting by species, such as a swift over the river or a pair of wagtails at the weir, with position and time filled in automatically.

controls.note: A swift over the river is a bird.

repos.name: pollboard
repos.readme:
# pollboard

Live polls for meetups. A Flask backend serves the poll API and a server-sent-events stream that pushes vote counts to the projector view.

controls.note: The backend is a Flask backend.

repos.name: brewlab
repos.readme:
# brewlab

Recipe manager for homebrewers. Follow a yeast starter from the first flask on the stir plate through to bottling, with gravity readings and tasting notes along the way.

controls.note: The flask holds a yeast starter.

repos.name: voxelnet-mini
repos.readme:
# voxelnet-mini

A compact 3D object detector for lidar point clouds. Data loading, model and training loop are all PyTorch, and checkpoints are standard `state_dict` files.

controls.note: The whole training stack is PyTorch.

repos.name: plumbline
repos.readme:
# plumbline

Job sheets for plumbers. Record each job's parts, time on site and any hot work, for example when a blow torch was used near timber, so the insurance log stays complete.

controls.note: A blow torch is a plumber's tool.

repos.name: sensorsift
repos.readme:
# sensorsift

Cleans raw readings from field sensors: resamples to fixed intervals, fills short gaps and drops spikes. Input and output are pandas DataFrames, so it slots into existing notebooks.

controls.note: The library operates on pandas DataFrames.

repos.name: zoo-feeding
repos.readme:
# zoo-feeding

Feeding rota for a small zoo. Keepers see which enclosures are due next, from bamboo deliveries for the giant pandas to live insects for the meerkats.

controls.note: Giant pandas are zoo animals.

repos.name: envcheck
repos.readme:
# envcheck

Validates environment variables against a declared spec at startup and fails fast with a readable message. Pure Python, no third-party dependencies.

controls.note: 'Pure Python' states the implementation language.

repos.name: vivarium-climate
repos.readme:
# vivarium-climate

Humidity and heat controller for reptile enclosures. Ships with presets for a green tree python, a bearded dragon and a crested gecko, and logs every reading to an SD card.

controls.note: A green tree python is a snake.

repos.name: backup-rotate
repos.readme:
# backup-rotate

Nightly backups with retention, implemented as a few POSIX shell scripts meant to run from cron. Keeps seven dailies and four weeklies by default.

controls.note: Implemented as shell scripts; Shell bytes agree.

repos.name: beachcomber
repos.readme:
# beachcomber

A field guide for rock-pool walks. Snap a photo of a crab, an anemone or a shell and it suggests a likely species with a short description and the best season to look.

controls.note: A shell found on a beach.

repos.name: moodmeter
repos.readme:
# moodmeter

Anonymous team mood check-ins. Built on Express, with a small React front end served from the same process.

controls.note: Explicitly built on Express with a React front end.

repos.name: tilecache
repos.readme:
# tilecache

Caching proxy for map tiles. The cache is implemented in Java and exposes a gRPC interface plus a small admin page.

controls.note: Explicitly implemented in Java.

repos.name: unsafe-audit
repos.readme:
# unsafe-audit

Extra lints for Rust crates that contain unsafe blocks. Installs as a cargo subcommand:

```
cargo install unsafe-audit
cargo unsafe-audit
```

controls.note: A cargo-installed subcommand linting Rust crates is itself a Rust crate.

repos.name: chartkit
repos.readme:
# chartkit

Adds a `.chartkit` accessor to pandas DataFrames for one-line exploratory charts:

```
df.chartkit.hist('latency_ms')
```

controls.note: Registering a DataFrame accessor requires pandas.

repos.name: metro-arrivals
repos.readme:
# metro-arrivals

Arrival predictions for a light-rail line.

## Background

The backend began life as a Ruby app. In 2023 it was ported to Elixir, and nothing from the original codebase remains in this repository.

controls.note: Ruby was the original backend, fully ported away.

repos.name: segmentor
repos.readme:
# segmentor

Splits scanned forms into fields.

Until v0.6 this package depended on torch for its tiny classifier. The model is now exported once and run with onnxruntime, so that dependency is gone.

controls.note: torch was a dependency before v0.6 and has been removed.

repos.name: notebridge
repos.readme:
# notebridge

Syncs notes between two desktop apps every few minutes.

## Next

An Express-based web dashboard is planned for the next release so you can see sync history from a browser.

controls.note: The Express dashboard is planned, not built.

repos.name: shapegen
repos.readme:
# shapegen

Procedural low-poly terrain generator in Go.

We would like to offer a Python package eventually so it can be scripted from notebooks; contributions welcome.

controls.note: A Python package is a wish for later.

repos.name: serverless-hello
repos.readme:
# serverless-hello

A hello-world cloud function. No Flask or other web framework: just the platform's handler signature and a JSON response.

controls.note: 'No Flask' explicitly excludes it.

repos.name: blinkui
repos.readme:
# blinkui

Lightweight widget toolkit that draws directly to a canvas element, without React or any virtual DOM layer in between.

controls.note: 'without React' excludes it.

repos.name: ironframe
repos.readme:
# ironframe

A dataframe library for Go with an API modelled on pandas: `Filter`, `GroupBy`, `Agg` and friends, but with static column types.

controls.note: pandas is the API model for a Go library.

repos.name: glint
repos.readme:
# glint

A linter for config files. Like the Rust compiler, it tries hard to give friendly error messages, with the offending snippet underlined and a suggested fix.

controls.note: The Rust compiler is a comparison for error-message style.

repos.name: webdev-reading-group
repos.readme:
# webdev-reading-group

Weekly notes from our reading group. This term we are going through the Flask documentation chapter by chapter; each week's summary is in `weeks/`.

controls.note: Summaries of another project's documentation, not a Flask project.

repos.name: tensor-cheatsheet
repos.readme:
# tensor-cheatsheet

Printable one-page cheat sheet of common PyTorch tensor operations, typeset in LaTeX. Only the LaTeX source and the rendered PDF live in this repo.

controls.note: Documents PyTorch's API but contains no code that runs it.

repos.name: release-notes-bot
repos.readme:
# release-notes-bot

Posts upstream release notes into a chat channel. Example post:

> **pathkit 4.2 released**: now requires Swift 5.9 and drops support for older toolchains.

Which upstream projects to watch is configured in `bot.yaml`.

controls.note: Swift appears only in a quoted upstream release note.

repos.name: license-audit
repos.readme:
# license-audit

Scans a project's dependencies and collects their licence texts. Excerpt from a report generated for a sample project:

> express: MIT licence, transitive dependency of `reports-ui`

Reports can be exported as Markdown or CSV.

controls.note: express is a line in sample output about a scanned project.

repos.name: statuspage-lite
repos.readme:
# statuspage-lite

Public status page with incident history and a subscribe-by-email form.

```
npm ci && npm start
```

controls.note: No README mention, but package.json depends on express.

repos.name: churn-baseline
repos.readme:
# churn-baseline

Customer churn baseline: feature preparation with pandas, a gradient-boosted classifier and a short evaluation report.

controls.note: Strong README claim matched by requirements.txt; Python bytes confirm the language.

repos.name: quickserve
repos.readme:
# quickserve

Express checkout for pop-up market stalls: scan, pay, done. Works on any phone with a camera.

controls.note: 'Express checkout' is ordinary, but package.json shows the express framework is used.

repos.name: corrosion-index
repos.readme:
# corrosion-index

Computes a corrosion risk index for buried pipelines from soil and moisture readings, highlighting segments where rust is likely to form first.

controls.note: README rust is corrosion, but the repository's code is Rust by bytes.

repos.name: panekit
repos.readme:
# panekit

Terminal pane manager written in Ruby. Save layouts, restore them per project.

repos.name: panekit-layouts
repos.readme:
# panekit-layouts

Community-contributed layout files for panekit.

controls.note: Ruby claim confirmed by Ruby bytes; Shell is about 8% so it also counts.

repos.name: taskfile-gen
repos.readme:
# taskfile-gen

Generates task-runner files from a short spec so every repo gets the same lint, test and release targets. Requires Python 3.11+.

controls.note: Requiring Python 3.11 to run implies a Python tool.

repos.name: csvline
repos.readme:
# csvline

Streaming CSV reader, in Swift, that never loads the whole file into memory. Rows arrive through an async sequence.

controls.note: README states the reader is written in Swift.

repos.name: nightvision-aug
repos.readme:
# nightvision-aug

Data augmentation for low-light images, implemented as torch transforms you can drop into any training pipeline.

## Example images

The sample photos in `examples/` were taken in a cellar lit only by a hand torch.

controls.note: 'torch transforms' is use, the later hand torch is ordinary; strongest class is use.

repos.name: serpent-sort
repos.readme:
# serpent-sort

Sorting algorithm visualiser. The mascot is a python that coils around the bars as they get sorted.

The visualiser itself is a small Python program using only the standard turtle module.

controls.note: The mascot python is a snake, but 'a small Python program' is use; strongest class is use.

repos.name: mailbatch
repos.readme:
# mailbatch

Bulk mail-merge tool written in Swift. Reads a template and a contact list and sends personalised messages in batches.

controls.note: README claims Swift but the repository is almost entirely Java bytes.

repos.name: embedcards
repos.readme:
# embedcards

Embeddable link-preview cards for blogs. Does not use React; drop one script tag on the page.

controls.note: README denies React while package.json depends on it.

repos.name: lanetimer
repos.readme:
# lanetimer

Timing app for school sports days. No need to shell out for timing gates: each lane judge uses a phone, and results sync to the announcer's laptop within a second.

controls.note: 'shell out' means to pay.

repos.name: chemlog
repos.readme:
# chemlog

React, record, repeat: a lab notebook for undergraduate chemistry practicals. Each experiment gets a page with reagents, observations and yields.

controls.note: Capitalised 'React' at sentence start refers to chemical reactions.
